simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to דָּג (H1709) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 19 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: דָּג (dâg) means a fish (often used collectively) First listed occurrence: 1Kgs 5 13.

definitions.full: H1709. dag דָּאג fish , compare דָּג below דגה . דָּג noun masculine Jonah 2:1 fish (Late Hebrew id. ) — דָּג 2:1 (twice in verse); Jonah 2:11 + Neh 13:16 Qr (Kt דָּאג ); דָּגִים 1Kin 5:13 6 t.; דְּגֵי Gen 9:2 7 t.; — fish of sea Jonah 2:1 (twice in verse); Jonah 2:11 (in 1:1 ׳ד גָּדוֺל ); Neh 13:16 ( דָּאג Kt דָּג article of Tyrian trade; only here collective, read perhaps דָּגָה ; or regard as late usage, compare converse דָּגָה of individual Jonah 2:2 ); — elsewhere always plural: as subject of Solomon's utterance 1Kin 5:13 ; fish-spear דגים צִלְצַל Job 40:31; most often הַיָּם דְּגֵי Gen 9:2 (P), Psa 8:9 ; Hosea 4:3 ; Zeph 1:3 ; Ezek 38:20 ; Job 12:8 (in all opposed to beasts & birds, & apparently used with them, + רֶמֶשׂ Ezekiel compare verb רמשׂ Genesis, for animal creation in General; also Hab 1:14 compare below); Num 11:22 (JE) of fish (with beasts) as food (compare Gen 9:2 f.) in simile of men ensnared, like fish taken in net ( מְצוֺדָה ) Eccl 9:12 compare Hab 1:14 ( הַיָּם דְּגֵי ); 4 t. הַדָּגִים שַׁעַר fish-gate 2Chr 33:14 ; Zeph 1:10 ; Neh 3:3 ; 12:39 (on situation compare שַׁעַר ).
definitions.rootNote: or (fully) דָּאג ; (Nehemiah 13:16), from 1711 ; a fish (as prolific); or perhaps rather from 1672 (as timid); but still better from 1672 (in the sense of squirming, i.e. moving by the vibratory action of the tail);
